course_name_original: Teoría de Estructuras y Construcciones Industriales I
course_name_en: Theory of Structures and Industrial Buildings I
prerequisites: Extension of Elasticity and Strength of Materials

learning_outcomes.text: Implementation of an industrial building and its relationship with its environment.
Understand the fundamentals of structural analysis, the organization and typology of industrial constructions, as well as the design and complete dimensioning of an industrial construction.
Design of basic metallic structural elements in industrial constructions.
Interpretation and proper use of current regulations in the design and calculation of metallic structures.

syllabus_topics: TOPIC 4. INDUSTRIAL BUILDINGS AND GENERAL ORGANIZATION
TOPIC 5. BENDING. BEAMS AND SLABS. PURLINS. OVERHEAD CRANES
TOPIC 6. COMPRESSION AND BUCKLING. COLUMNS. BRACING
TOPIC 11. INTRODUCTION TO FOUNDATIONS. ISOLATED FOOTINGS
Individual work analyzing videos or scientific articles in English related to the competencies to be developed by this course.

assessment_methods.method: Short answer tests (theoretical part of continuous assessment tests)
Development tests (practical part of continuous assessment tests)

assessment_rules: All students are subject to continuous assessment in the first call, unless they opt for single assessment. Continuous assessment consists of four theoretical-practical tests, each weighted 1/4 of the final grade. A minimum score of 2.50 points is required in each test. If all tests score 2.50 or higher, the average is calculated; if this average is 5.00 or higher, the course is passed. If any test scores below 2.50, the final grade is the arithmetic mean of all tests, capped at 3.00 points. For single assessment, a single theoretical-practical test is given, graded 0-10 points.
